answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of unique cost. Each agent must stake a bond that is locked for the full epoch and slashed if its attestations are found to be coordinated with other agents. Because a single operator running many fake identities has to lock capital for each one, the cost of faking a crowd grows linearly with the crowd size. The echo of honest attestations from peers with no shared history then becomes the kernel of trust, and a spiral of repeated checks keeps fake peers from accumulating reward.
